acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). The preceding protocol's sub-condition (c) - candidate successes strictly exceeding cumulative - is NOT carried over as a graded sub-condition in this protocol: it was the preceding cycle's headline test of a different selected limitation (engagement sparsity), it failed on both cohorts on the strength of a single opposed_count == 0 blind-spot state per cohort, and grading it again here would conflate two distinct limitations in one experiment, contrary to the one-measurable-limitation cycle. Cumulative's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside this criterion in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. This cycle's headline test is criterion 5.

acceptance_criteria.name: recovery_engagement_preserved_and_selective
acceptance_criteria.rule: Graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY (no TEST outcomes), per cohort: (a) the recovery branch is TAKEN (joint_count >= 1, recovery armed, acting source retained_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 return-A onset seed-checkpoint states (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds) - the low edge of this protocol's design interval of approx 3-4 of 6 under the expiry condition, materially more than the pooled candidate's 1 of 6 and below the unexpired joint candidate's graded 5 of 6, as derived in threshold_justification; AND (b) the recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 B1 onset seed-checkpoint states. B2 and control engagement counts are reported, not graded under this criterion (B2 non-recovery is a pre-registered expectation, and control engagement is graded downstream under criterion 6). Would-fire-but-disarmed counts at onset are reported alongside: they distinguish over-expiry (would-fire high, taken low) from joint-test silence (would-fire low).

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint protocol. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. Carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded joint candidate FAILed its checkpoint-32 criterion on both cohorts, and this cycle exists to answer that failure. Per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (the campaign's selected measurable form for this cycle: k=32 productivity restored to within 8 successes of recent8; the joint candidate's gaps were -19 development and -9 additional), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive or abstained) in at most 1 state - the direct records-level measure that the gate's authority has actually expired late, as distinct from its downstream totals happening to pass. Sub-condition (c)'s design expectation is approx 0-1 states per cohort (see threshold_justification); the graded joint candidate took 2 (development) and 1 (additional) such states at checkpoint 32, but its development total was driven by exactly those 2 states, so (c) at most 1 together with (b) is the falsifiable form of the expiry claim.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_downstream_selectivity
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 5, the retained-recovery protocol's criterion 6, and the joint protocol's criterion 6. Expiry-flag values on the control arm are recorded and reported; the flag itself is not graded here, the downstream totals are.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, joint_count, opposed_count, matched_count, concordant_count, archive_matched_count, the full expiry record incl. per-span local/archive majorities, comparable/disagreeing counts, stable_disagreement flag, per-event last-8 archive-concordance flags, recent_concordant_count, per-branch armed and would-fire flags, branch taken, recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule (now including its expiry condition) alone
baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; engagement, onset, and checkpoint-32 comparisons in the report (its totals are reference points, not PASS/FAIL comparators in the criteria, whose bounds are absolute or against recent8/guard/cumulative/frozen_A as named)
baselines.name: joint_concordance_recovery
baselines.role: JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Failed): identical acting model, identical immediate signal, identical archive, identical joint recovery test, identical abstention branch, differing ONLY in that its branches have NO expiry condition. This is the decisive comparison for this experiment: candidate-vs-joint-candidate differences isolate the authority bound alone, at onset (criteria 1-4) and at checkpoint 32 (criterion 5).

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; return-A and checkpoint-32 reference comparisons in the report (not a PASS/FAIL comparator in this protocol's criteria - see the grading note on criterion 1)
baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. Plain cumulative retention dominated the pooled retained-recovery candidate and trailed the joint candidate's firing states not at all (identical per firing state); it remains the strongest simple retained comparator and is reported at every checkpoint, including at return-A and checkpoint 32.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons
baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory (graded Demonstrated): the candidate's own immediate signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response, released by checkpoint 32 on both of its cohorts by window-sliding. Criteria 1, 3, and 4 hold the candidate to the guard's harm levels on the same cohort.

baselines.name: evidence_opposition_retained_recovery
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, the pooled both-events candidate (graded Failed): the engagement-sparsity reference point.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criterion 1 comparison
baselines.name: frozen_A
baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated. The recovery target reference at return_A: what pure retained pre-switch knowledge scores there.

baselines.name: recent32
baselines.role: Relation model on the last 32 observed events.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; preceding-learner comparison
baselines.name: gated_archive_prequential
baselines.role: GatedArchivePrequentialMemory (graded Failed / regression): the earlier archive-routing candidate.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; productivity floor reference
baselines.name: always_abstain
baselines.role: Abstains on every TEST task: 0 successes, 0 harmful actions, all tasks failed-by-abstention. The trivially safe control.

baselines.name: untrained_random
baselines.role: Independent seeded random TEST action policy; gathers no training outcomes.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint, labeled privileged
baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle
baselines.role: PRIVILEGED reference only: knows the expected hidden rule (not the realized stochastic flip). Never a realizable baseline and never counted in any PASS/FAIL comparison.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 6 per stage per cohort at checkpoints 2 and 4, and 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32.

budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, and joint protocols. Abstention disarmed late is this experiment's intended release mechanism, not a budget violation.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The disarmed-abstention tradeoff at return onset (expected failure mode 2) is charged against these criteria, not excused from them.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Over-expiry at return onset (pre-registered as the central risk): the corroboration condition is met at only approx 0.55-0.70 of return-A onset states by design, so recovery engagement may fall to 2-3 of 6 states and criterion 2 (floor 3 of 6) and criterion 1 may FAIL even though the expiry condition works exactly as designed at checkpoint 32. That outcome would show the authority bound costs more onset engagement than this simulator's return evidence can pay for - an informative, pre-registered result, not a protocol defect.

Abstention disarmed at return onset: because the local segment at a return is the reversed segment, the stable-disagreement flag is set there and the abstention fallback cannot fire at return-A onset states. Non-engaging return states therefore act through stale recent8 instead of abstaining, raising return-A and pooled onset harm relative to the joint candidate; criteria 3 and 4 may FAIL on this tradeoff even if engagement holds.

Residual late false recovery: a late acting window containing two flip-back events (design approx 0.28 of late states) re-arms recovery, and if the newest window also carries a joint event the stale archive route fires for a full checkpoint, as in the graded joint candidate. Criterion 5's records sub-condition (at most 1 non-recent8 branch state at checkpoint 32) and its productivity sub-condition grade exactly this residual.

Local-majority noise keeps the flag unset late: the local window holds only ~2-4 events per span, so at some late states the comparable-span disagreement may fall to or below half by sampling noise, leaving the branches armed at checkpoint 32 on those states. The flag's design firing probability late is approx 0.90, not 1; scattered late armed states are expected and are graded through criterion 5's totals, not treated as implementation errors.

opposed_count == 0 return-A blind spot (recorded, NOT this cycle's selected limitation): a return state whose newest events agree with the already-partly-slid reference window cannot engage recovery under the joint test, expired or not. It accounted for the entire exceed-cumulative deficit in the preceding experiment (-4 / -12). It is reported from the records in this experiment and is deliberately not graded away and not repaired here; repairing it is a separate hypothesis requiring its own protocol.

Return-A archive harm at scale: as in the preceding experiment, archive play in firing states carries nonzero harm (design approx 4-8 per firing state); with several firing states pooled return-A harm can land above the 60-percent-of-recent8 ceiling (the preceding candidate: 40 vs ceiling 37.8 on development) and fail criterion 4.

Stationary expiry noise: on the control arm the local and archive rules agree, so the disagreement flag should stay unset (design probability well under 0.05 per state); if sampling noise sets it at some control states, the only effect is disarming branches whose engagement on stationary evidence was downstream-harmless in the preceding experiment, so criterion 6 should be unaffected - but every control-state flag value is recorded and reported.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, the graded retained-recovery candidate, and the graded joint candidate.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, expiry records - comparable/disagreeing span counts, stable-disagreement flag, per-event last-8 archive-concordance flags, recent_concordant_count, per-branch armed and would-fire flags - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive). (2) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed, abstain (choose returns None), exactly the graded guard's protective response. (3) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Onset protection and late release are separated by evidence the newest window does not contain. While no stable archive-disagreeing local segment exists, the stream has not yet established a current rule the archive lacks, so both protective branches keep the authority the graded joint candidate gave them - this covers B1 onset (local window still the original rule, agreeing with the archive), B2 onset (local window still the return-A segment, agreeing with the archive), and stationary evidence (local and archive agree throughout). At a return onset the local segment IS the intervening reversed segment and disagrees with the archive, so abstention is disarmed there by design (recovery, not abstention, is the return response; a non-engaging return state acts through recent8 rather than abstaining - a pre-registered tradeoff, graded under criteria 3 and 4), while recovery stays armed through the corroboration condition: a genuine return's newest events are themselves archive-concordant, so the last-8 archive-concordant count reaches the threshold of 2 from the newest window alone in expectation. Long after a switch to a rule the archive does not hold, the local window is a stable current-rule segment disagreeing with the archive on most comparable spans, and an isolated flip-back carries fewer than 2 archive-concordant events in its last 8 in expectation, so both branches are disarmed and the learner acts through recent8, which has by then adapted - the release the graded guard achieved by window-sliding, extended to the archive route whose window never slides.
fixed_parameters.expiry_condition: NEW, the single changed element of this experiment. Two quantities are computed from the observed reported stream only, at every decision, using the SAME span-majority machinery (strictly-highest reported class among events of equal span; tie or empty gives null; only progress/damage majorities are comparable): (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT. The local window is the last 26 observed events (the reference window plus the newest window, indices N-26 .. N-1). For each distinct span value s present in the local window, let local_majority(s) be the strictly-highest reported class among local-window events of span s and archive_majority(s) the strictly-highest reported class among archive events (events[:N-26]) of span s. Span s is COMPARABLE if both majorities are progress or damage, and DISAGREEING if comparable and the two majorities differ. Let comparable_span_count = C and disagreeing_span_count = D. The stable-disagreement flag is set iff C >= 1 AND D * 2 > C (a strict majority of comparable spans disagree). (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE. For each of the last 8 observed events, the event is counted archive-concordant iff it is archive-matched and its reported class equals archive_majority(span(event)), using the SAME current archive as above (not a per-position archive). recent_concordant_count is in 0..8. BRANCH AUTHORITY: the ABSTENTION branch is ARMED iff the stable-disagreement flag is NOT set. The RECOVERY branch is ARMED iff the stable-disagreement flag is NOT set OR recent_concordant_count >= 2. When a branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever its trigger count says; a decision that would have taken a disarmed branch falls through to the next branch in the decision order, exactly as if its trigger had not fired, and the record carries both the would-have-fired flag and the armed flag so the expiry's effect is graded from the records alone. No other input enters the condition: no fitted probability, no phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded evidence-opposition guard, the graded retained-recovery candidate, and the graded joint candidate, reused unchanged and not re-tuned: newest window = last 2 observed events; reference window = the 24 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-26 .. N-3). For each newest event, the reference expectation is the strictly-highest reported outcome class among reference events of equal span (tie or empty gives null); an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different. opposed_count in 0..2. No fitted probabilities anywhere in any signal.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded joint candidate, unchanged: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT (per the unchanged archive test) AND reference-OPPOSED (per the unchanged immediate signal) - both flags on the SAME event. joint_count is the number of joint newest events (0..2).
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: Both signals together require a 2-event newest window, a full 24-event reference window, and at least 1 archive event: at least 27 observed events. Below 27 events neither signal is evaluable and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so this fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose). The recovery model never includes the reference window or the newest window.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded retained-recovery and joint candidates: every observed event BEFORE the reference window, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. It is not a snapshot, not phase-segmented, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates and the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). Span-majority reliability: the archive holds ~214+ events at every graded checkpoint (~20+ per span value across the engineered span bands), so its per-span majorities are the majority rule's class with probability near 1. The local window holds 26 events (~2-4 per span), so a local per-span majority follows the local segment's rule with design probability approx 0.75-0.90 per span (majority of 2-4 samples each agreeing with the segment rule at the composed agreement rate approx 0.84 after the 0.1625 disagreement rate from 1/8 stochastic + 1/20 report flips). Where local and archive rules are the SAME, a comparable span disagrees only when the local majority errs: per-span disagreement approx 0.10-0.25, so a strict-majority disagreement flag over the comparable spans (typically 6-10) fires with design probability well under 0.05 - the branches stay armed at B1/B2 onset and on stationary evidence. Where the local segment's rule is the REVERSE of the archive's, per-span disagreement is approx 0.75-0.90 and the flag fires with design probability approx 0.90 or higher - the flag reliably marks a stable reversed local segment, at a return onset and late in B1/B2 alike, which is why recovery authority there is carried by the corroboration condition instead. Corroboration arithmetic: a newest event at a genuine return is archive-concordant with design probability approx 0.65-0.70 (non-neutral span fraction approx 0.8 x agreement approx 0.84, as derived in the preceding protocols); an event following the reversed rule is archive-concordant only as a flip-back, approx 0.13 (flip agreement approx 0.1625 x non-neutral approx 0.8). At return onset checkpoints 2 and 4 the last 8 events are the newest 2 return events plus 6 reversed events (at k=2) or the newest 2 plus a 4-return / 2-reversed mix (at k=4, the last 8 contain 4 return events): expected recent_concordant_count approx 2.1 (k=2) to approx 3.2 (k=4), so the >= 2 threshold is met with design probability approx 0.55-0.70 per return-A onset state; combined with the joint test's per-state engagement (graded 5 of 6 for the unexpired gate, per-state design approx 0.70-0.80), recovery engagement per return-A onset state is approx 0.45-0.60, i.e. approx 3 of 6 states - hence criterion 2's engagement floor is set at 3 of 6 for this experiment, at the low edge of that design interval, and a criterion-2 FAIL from over-expiry is a pre-registered informative outcome (expected failure mode 1), not a protocol defect to be repaired after seeing scores. Late in a reversed stage, all 8 acting-window events follow the current reversed rule: expected recent_concordant_count approx 1.0, reaching >= 2 with design probability approx 0.28; recovery additionally requires a joint event in the newest window (approx 0.25 per state late), so a late false recovery requires both, design probability approx 0.05-0.08 per late state - hence criterion 5's records sub-condition allows at most 1 non-recent8 branch state among the 9 checkpoint-32 switch-stage states per cohort. The abstention threshold (opposed_count == 2) and recovery threshold (joint_count >= 1) are carried over UNCHANGED from the graded joint candidate; the only new thresholds are the strict-majority disagreement rule (D * 2 > C, the weakest strict form, chosen so the flag is a majority statement rather than a fitted constant) and the corroboration count >= 2 (the smallest count that an isolated single flip cannot reach on its own).

candidate.name: BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, the graded EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, and the graded JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

capability_under_test: Gate persistence without expiry: whether a recovery/abstention gate whose authority is bounded to the onset window - by an evidence-derived condition, not by any phase, stage, or checkpoint information the learner cannot see - can preserve the graded joint test's onset engagement and harm profile (return-A engagement at materially more states than the pooled candidate, pooled onset harm at or below the evidence-opposition guard's level) while restoring checkpoint-32 productivity to within 8 successes of recent8, against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, the graded retained-recovery candidate, and the graded joint-concordance candidate as baselines. Priority 1 items 2 + 3 joined to item 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge and first-contact overconfidence.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 are the graded onset window; 8 and 16 report persistence costs; 32 grades release, and in this experiment criterion 5 at checkpoint 32 is the PRIMARY criterion - the graded joint candidate failed exactly there on both cohorts. Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations). Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit.
grading.failed: Criterion 5 FAILs on the additional cohort, or any of criteria 1-4 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary. Criterion 5 is reported first among the criteria in the grading report, as this experiment's primary criterion.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, routing, and now expiry rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, joint test, disagreement and corroboration conditions, and decision rule are all designer-supplied. A PASS would demonstrate evidence-bounded gate authority - onset protection that expires on observed evidence - in this simulator only, not general regime identification (the archive is global and unsegmented; B2 recovery is pre-registered as not expected), not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criterion 5 and criterion 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 1, 2, 3, 4, or 6 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the candidate's checkpoint-32 successes fall below the graded joint candidate's checkpoint-32 deficit pattern (i.e. below recent8 - 19 on either cohort, the joint candidate's worse cohort gap), or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.

hypothesis: The joint candidate's two branches stay armed indefinitely because their triggers are evaluated on the newest 2 events alone, and a newest window that is archive-concordant and reference-opposed is locally identical whether it is the first evidence of a genuine return or an isolated flip-back noise event long after a switch, when the recent window has already adapted to the current rule and the archive route is purely harmful. What differs between those situations IS visible in the observed stream, in two places the newest window does not look at. (1) Segment stability: at an onset, the local window (the last 26 events) still follows the pre-switch rule on most spans, so its span majorities AGREE with the retained archive's span majorities wherever the pre-switch rule is the archive's rule, or - at a return onset - the local window is the intervening reversed segment, whose disagreement with the archive is exactly the situation the recovery branch exists for. Long after a switch to a rule the archive does not hold, the local window has become a stable segment of the CURRENT rule: its span majorities disagree with the archive's on a strict majority of comparable spans. A stable local segment that the archive disagrees with is positive evidence that the current rule is not the archive's rule and has already been in place for a full local window - the onset window has passed. (2) Return corroboration inside the acting window: at a genuine return onset (checkpoints 2 and 4), the newest joint events are not isolated in the recent past - counting the last 8 events against the CURRENT archive, a return onset carries the newest 2 archive-concordant events themselves, so the archive-concordant count in the last 8 reaches 2 by construction of the return (design expectation approx 2.1: the newest 2 at the per-event concordant rate approx 0.65-0.70 plus flip-back concordance among the 6 preceding reversed events at approx 0.13 each). An isolated late flip carries design expectation approx 1.0 archive-concordant events in its last 8 (8 events at the flip-back concordant rate approx 0.13), reaching 2 only when a second flip happens to fall in the same window (design probability approx 0.28). Bounding the branches' authority by these two evidence-derived conditions - abstention armed only while no stable archive-disagreeing local segment exists; recovery armed while no such segment exists OR the last-8 archive-concordant count reaches 2 - should therefore keep onset behavior (where either the local window still agrees with the archive, or the return corroboration is present) while disarming the branches late (where a stable archive-disagreeing segment exists and the joint event is an isolated flip), restoring checkpoint-32 productivity toward recent8. The residual failure modes are pre-registered, not hidden: a late window containing two flip-backs can still arm recovery (approx 0.28 of late states before the newest-window joint test is even applied, and the joint test must also fire), and at a return onset the abstention fallback is disarmed by design (the local segment is the reversed segment, which disagrees with the archive), so a return state where recovery does not engage acts through recent8 instead of abstaining.

EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD (docs/EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD.md, graded Demonstrated 2026-10-29, cohorts 312003-family / 313001-family now INSPECTED): the abstention-only guard, whose reference window slides past the switch, released fully by checkpoint 32 on both cohorts (0/144 abstentions, successes identical to recent8) - release by checkpoint 32 is attainable in this simulator when the protective mechanism's authority is tied to a sliding evidence window. permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, checkpoint value, stage position, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its concordance tests, its expiry condition, its recovery model, or its checkpoint record. In particular the expiry condition is computed from reported events and their spans only: the learner has no access to how many events have elapsed since any switch, and no threshold in this protocol is a count of post-switch events.
priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4. This experiment builds directly on the graded joint-concordance failure at checkpoint 32: the joint recovery test solved onset engagement (5 of 6 return-A onset states on both cohorts) but the recovery and abstention branches remain armed at every checkpoint, so long after onset a single spurious joint event can still route the learner to the stale global archive for a full checkpoint. This cycle changes exactly one thing - the AUTHORITY of the two gate branches, bounded by an evidence-derived expiry condition computed from the observed stream alone - and asks whether the onset profile survives while checkpoint-32 productivity is restored. This cycle's headline criterion is therefore the checkpoint-32 release/productivity criterion (criterion 5), graded as primary.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the six graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_retained_recovery, joint_concordance_recovery, and the abstention guard counted once) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the acting model, the immediate opposition signal, the retained archive, the archive concordance definition, the joint recovery test, the recovery model, and every window size of the graded joint candidate are reused EXACTLY as frozen in the joint-concordance protocol (newest window 2, reference window 24, archive events[:N-26], opposed_count / concordant_count / joint_count definitions unchanged, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention threshold opposed_count == 2). The single new element - the branch-authority (expiry) condition built from the local-window/archive span-majority disagreement count and the last-8 archive-concordant count, with thresholds derived a priori in candidate.fixed_parameters.threshold_justification - is informed only by the preceding experiment's published graded aggregates and per-cell persistence records (its limitation evidence), never by any score of this experiment (none exist).
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures recovery-branch selectivity: false engagement, false abstention, and lost productivity when nothing changed.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).
